newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief congratulates Clinton on victory.
newsitem.headline: UN chief congratulates Clinton on victory.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Wednesday congratulated President Bill Clinton on his election victory, and U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright said Washington still wanted the U.N. chief to step down.
U.N. spokesman Ahmad Fawzi said the secretary-general had sent Clinton a letter congratulating him on his "historic electoral victory."
Boutros-Ghali said he hoped the United States and the United Nations could work together in the period ahead to further world peace and prosperity, Fawzi reported.
The Clinton administration, with little support from any other country, has vowed to block Boutros-Ghali's bid for a second five-year term, saying he has not done enough to reform the world body.
Asked about Boutros-Ghali's re-election, Albright said: "As part of building the bridge to the 21st Century, we want a new leader for the United Nations."
She said the Clinton administration planned to work with the new Republican-dominated Congress to get more support for the United Nations.

The United States owes the United Nations over $1.4 billion in past dues and for peacekeeping operations, and this has lessened U.S. influence. While Washington can veto Boutros-Ghali's re-election bid, any successor it chooses would be automatically opposed by other key members.
